newsitem.title: CROATIA: Bosnia court rejects Croat appeal over Mostar vote.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia court rejects Croat appeal over Mostar vote.

text.p: The Bosnian Supreme Court has rejected a Bosnian Croat appeal to annul local elections in the southern Bosnian city of Mostar, a European Union official said on Thursday.

"The court found the case was outside its jurisdiction and rejected the Croat appeal at a session on Wednesday," the EU spokesman in Mostar Dragan Gasic said. "We just got the ruling and are studying it now."
The leading Bosnian Croat party, the Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ), complained to the EU ombudsman about alleged irregularities in the municipal poll last June after it lost to Moslem rivals.
HDZ demanded the elections be partially annulled and repeated.

The ombudsman ruled the violations too minor to affect the outcome and confirmed the election results. The Croats then took their case to the Supreme Court of the Moslem-Croat Federation, one of Bosnia's two constituent parts.

Mostar's elected HDZ officials also refused to join the city assembly and the federation government before the issue was resolved, sparking a political crisis that threatened to shatter the fragile Moslem-Croat alliance.

But the Supreme Court, consisting of three judges -- one from each of Bosnia's three ethnic groups -- ruled on Wednesday that the federation court had no jurisdiction over the case, and the EU ombudsman had the legal right to judge the matter.
"We welcome the Court's ruling, and hope it will contribute towards the normal work of the city council," Gasic said.
There was no immediate reaction from Bosnian Croat officials. The majority moslem Party of Democratic Action won a five-seat majority on the 37-seat local city assembly.
Mostar has been sharply divided into Moslem and Croat sectors since 1993-94, when the two sides fought a bitter war for control of the town.
